summary: Describes extensions to the pseudowire control protocol so segments of a multi-segment pseudowire can be placed dynamically among provider edge routers. It also updates RFC 6073 by setting the Length field of a particular sub-TLV to 14.

eli5.summary: A long pipe made from several pieces across networks needs to be connected. This lets the routers pick where the pieces join automatically.

questions: how are s-pes selected for a pseudowire
how do t-pes choose the active role
subtitle: How provider edge routers can pick the hops of a multi-segment pseudowire on their own instead of being configured by hand.

tldr.problem: A multi-segment pseudowire is a chain of pseudowire segments across several network domains. RFC 6073 requires every switching router on the chain to be configured by hand with the details of each segment.
tldr.mechanism: Each pseudowire endpoint gets a globally unique address (AII Type 2). Switching routers look up the target address in a pseudowire routing table, filled by static routes or by BGP, and use LDP to set up the next segment hop by hop.
tldr.outcome: The network can now choose the switching points automatically. The RFC also adds an optional Bandwidth TLV and three LDP status codes, and corrects the length of the PW Switching Point PE sub-TLV type 0x06 to 14.

today: RFC 7267 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2014. It has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC, and it updates RFC 6073 by setting the Length of the PW Switching Point PE Sub-TLV type 0x06 to 14.

sections.title: Multi-Segment Pseudowires and Their Placement
sections.content:
A pseudowire (PW) emulates a point-to-point service across a packet network. RFC 5254 gives the requirements for stretching pseudowires across several Packet Switched Network (PSN) domains, and a multi-segment pseudowire (MS-PW) is a set of two or more contiguous PW segments that behave as a single point-to-point PW. The architecture is in RFC 5659.

A single-segment PW is set up with the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) as in RFC 4447. RFC 6073 covers stitching segments together but needs each switching router to be configured with the details of every segment. This document extends those procedures so that segments can be dynamically placed, reusing existing TLVs and the guidelines of RFC 5036.

The RFC adds some terms. The ST-PE is the terminating provider edge (T-PE) that takes the active signaling role. The TT-PE is the T-PE that takes the passive role. PW routing means dynamic placement of the segments plus automatic selection of switching PEs (S-PEs). Dynamic placement of point-to-multipoint PWs is outside the scope.

The RFC applies only to MPLS PSNs using the Generalized PWid FEC element (FEC 129). Use over an IP PSN with L2TPv3 is left for further study, and the RFC does not specify LDP use in an inter-AS environment.
sections.eli5: A long pipe made of several short pieces needs someone to decide which pieces to join. This document lets the routers decide, so people do not have to.

sections.title: Globally Unique Pseudowire Addresses
sections.content:
For dynamic placement, the attachment circuit identifiers must be globally unique so a PW can be found and managed. Individual globally unique addresses MUST be allocated to all the attachment circuits (ACs) and S-PEs of an MS-PW.

AC addresses use AII Type 2 from RFC 5003, made of a Global ID, a Prefix and an AC ID. The same AII type MUST be used for all segments, and the AII MUST be globally unique across all PSNs spanned by the MS-PW. Usually the same Global ID and Prefix are given to all ACs on one T-PE, but that is not a strict rule. The local AC's address and the far-end AC's address are the Source AII (SAII) and Target AII (TAII).

Each S-PE MUST also have an address, with at least one Attachment Identifier made of the Global ID and Prefix only, so it can fill in the PW Switching Point PE TLV. An S-PE that can do dynamic MS-PW signaling but has no address MUST answer a Label Mapping message with a Label Release carrying the status code Resources Unavailable (0x38).
sections.eli5: Every mailbox and every sorting depot needs its own full address, unique in the whole world, so letters never get confused.

sections.title: Pseudowire Routing
sections.content:
When an S-PE gets a Label Mapping message whose TAII is not local, it looks the TAII up in a PW AII routing table. If the lookup gives the IP address of a next-hop PE, the S-PE starts setting up the next segment. If it gives nothing, the setup MUST fail and a Label Release with the status AII Unreachable is returned. All PEs capable of dynamic path selection MUST build such a table.

The address has a Global ID, a 32-bit Prefix and a 32-bit AC ID. As with classless IPv4 routes, an 8-bit length mask from 0 to 96 says how many most significant bits count, and the route with the longest match wins. A PE MAY be given static routes; the usual example is a default route with Global ID, Prefix and AC ID all 0 and prefix length 0.

Routes can also be spread with BGP and its multiprotocol extensions (RFC 4760). The NLRI is carried in MP_REACH_NLRI and MP_UNREACH_NLRI using AFI 25 and SAFI 6. Only the T-PE Global ID, Prefix and prefix length need advertising, because the source T-PE already knows the far AC ID from provisioning. The multiprotocol BGP neighbor topology MUST coincide with the topology of T-PEs and S-PEs.

In the NLRI, the Length field has a minimum of 96 bits (except for the default route, encoded as a 0-length prefix) and a maximum of 160 bits. Lengths of 128 to 159 bits are invalid, because the AC ID cannot be aggregated, and such advertisements MUST be rejected as having a bad packet format.
sections.eli5: Each depot keeps a list that says which depot to hand a parcel to next, based on the start of the address. The longest matching entry wins.

sections.title: LDP Signaling and Bandwidth
sections.content:
No new LDP signaling components are needed for dynamic MS-PWs, but some optional extensions are defined. To keep quality of service, a PSN tunnel with enough class of service and bandwidth MUST be selected on each segment. With dynamic selection the next hop is not configured at the S-PE, so the bandwidth must be signaled. This is done with the optional PW Bandwidth TLV (type 0x096E), which carries a Forward and a Reverse SENDER_TSPEC from RFC 2210 and has a value length of 64.

An S/T-PE that receives the TLV MUST request the resources from the PSN once the next hop is chosen. If resources towards the previous hop are missing, the PSN MAY allocate more, or the S-PE MAY set up another tunnel. Otherwise a Label Release with Bandwidth resources unavailable MUST be returned.

Only one T-PE may start signaling, so both directions take one path. The two T-PEs compare SAII and TAII as unsigned integers, field by field (Global ID, then Prefix, then AC ID). A T-PE where SAII is greater takes the active role (ST-PE) and the other the passive role (TT-PE); equal values are a configuration error.

On a Label Mapping, an S-PE checks whether the FEC is installed. If it is, and the message came from the same peer the forward mapping was sent to, it is the reverse direction. If it came from a different peer, it is released with PW Loop Detected. Otherwise it is the forward direction: find the next hop, check or set up PSN tunnels, allocate a label, install the FEC and send the Label Mapping onward. The reverse direction reuses the LDP sessions of the forward path. When a route has several next hops, a selection such as CRC32 on the FEC TLV may be used so each PW has one next hop.
sections.eli5: Only one end starts the trip, so the parcel does not take two different roads. Each depot also reserves enough room on the truck for the parcel.

sections.title: Handling Failures
sections.content:
PSN tunnel failures MUST be handled by PSN mechanisms such as MPLS fast reroute (RFC 4090). If the tunnel cannot be restored, the S-PE SHOULD follow Section 10 of RFC 6073. Defects inside an S-PE follow RFC 6073 as well.

A T-PE or S-PE may receive an unsolicited Label Release with failure codes such as PW Loop Detected, Resources Unavailable or AII Unreachable. A T-PE that gets one is RECOMMENDED to try again right away, but it MUST throttle retries with an exponential backoff if setups keep being released, and is RECOMMENDED to notify an operator. An S-PE that gets one MUST tear down both segments and SHOULD pass the status code along.

An established MS-PW is generally not affected by next-hop changes in AII reachability. A T-PE or S-PE MAY choose to tear it down (an optional and likely disruptive step, with the status AII Unreachable), and PW Redundancy (RFC 6718) MAY be used to keep the service connected. A reachability change in the reverse direction has no effect.
sections.eli5: If a road is closed, the depot tells the sender and the sender tries again, waiting longer each time so it does not flood the depot with requests.

sections.title: OAM and the Switching Point Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The OAM procedures of RFC 6073 can also be used for dynamically placed MS-PWs, and a PW Switching Point PE TLV records the switching points the PW passes through. Because these PWs have no per-segment PWid, each segment is identified by the address of the adjacent S-PE(s) together with the SAII and TAII.

For this the sub-TLV type 0x06 (L2 PW address of PW Switching Point) MUST be used instead of type 0x01, once per switching point. The RFC also fixes an error: RFC 6073 gave the length as 12, but the length value MUST be set to 14. This is the sense in which RFC 7267 updates RFC 6073.
sections.eli5: Each depot signs the parcel's tracking sheet. This note fixes a typo about how long the signature line is.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extensions do not change the security considerations of RFC 4447 and RFC 6073, but those still apply. Section 13 of RFC 6073 covers LDP across administrative boundaries, including integrity and authentication of LDP control messages.

Dynamic selection lets the network choose the S-PEs that forward packets. An operator can check the chosen path with the Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) trace mechanisms of RFC 6073 to confirm it is not an added security risk. The protocols used to distribute AII reachability may have their own security considerations, which are outside this document.
sections.eli5: Because the routers now pick the route, the owner should be able to check which depots the parcel passed through and make sure they are trusted.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA corrected the entry for sub-TLV type 0x06 in the Pseudowire Switching Point PE sub-TLV Type registry to length 14. It assigned LDP TLV type 0x096E to the Bandwidth TLV, and three LDP status codes: 0x00000037 (Bandwidth resources unavailable), 0x00000038 (Resources Unavailable) and 0x00000039 (AII Unreachable). It also allocated BGP SAFI value 6 for the NLRI used for dynamic placement of multi-segment pseudowires.
sections.eli5: The official number registry got new entries so every router uses the same code for the same message.
